q: What is Q-Drive?
a: Q-Drive is a private drive Q-App on Qortal, published under the name Q-Drive. Your files, their names and your folders are encrypted on your device before anything is published to QDN, so only your account, and people you share with, can open them. It has folders, search, stars, a trash, previews for most file types, sharing, and a Notes tab for notes and to-do lists.

q: How do I open Q-Drive?
a: Q-Drive runs inside Qortal Hub on a computer or Qortal GO on a phone. Open it from the apps list there, or with the link qortal://APP/Q-Drive. In a normal web browser it only shows a note asking you to open it in Hub or GO, because it needs your Qortal account to encrypt and publish.

q: What do I need before I can use Q-Drive?
aliases: can i use q-drive without a name
a: You need a Qortal account signed in to Hub or GO, a registered name, and a little QORT for fees. Q-Drive keeps your encrypted files under your Qortal name, so with no name it asks you to register one in Hub (1.25 QORT), wait for it to confirm, then come back. The Notes tab works without a name, but your notes then stay on that device only.

q: How do I create my drive in Q-Drive?
a:
1. Open Q-Drive in Hub or GO and let it ask Hub which account to use.
2. On "Create your private drive", choose whether to set a vault passphrase now (optional extra protection).
3. Tap "Create my drive (0.01 QORT)" and confirm in Hub.
If you used Q-Drive with this name before, tap Look again first: your node may still be catching up, and Q-Drive won't make a second drive while it can't tell.

q: How much does Q-Drive cost to use?
a: There is no subscription. Every publish costs 0.01 QORT per resource and always waits for your tap: creating the drive is 0.01, each file is 0.01 plus 0.01 to update your file list (two files cost 0.03), saving other changes is 0.01, and a share is 0.02 (0.03 with a Q-Mail notice). Opening and downloading your own files costs nothing. Hub shows the cost and asks you to confirm each time.

q: How do I add files to Q-Drive?
a: Use New, then Publish files (or Publish folder), or the + button on a phone. On a computer you can also drag files onto the drive ("Drop to publish"). Q-Drive shows the cost, encrypts each file on your device, then publishes it to QDN after you confirm in Hub. Q-Drive says "publish" rather than "upload" because the files go to your node and the peer network, not to a company server.

q: Why do my Q-Drive changes need Save changes?
a: Renames, moves, new folders, stars, notes on files and the trash are changes to your encrypted file list, so they stay on the device until you save. The bar at the bottom shows how many changes are waiting; Save publishes your encrypted file list once (0.01 QORT) after you confirm in Hub. Discard puts your drive back to how it was last saved.

q: How do I make a new folder in Q-Drive?
a: In My Drive or one of its folders, choose New, then New folder (on a phone, the + button). On a computer you can also right-click or double-tap empty space to open the New menu there. Folder names are encrypted with your drive. The new folder is a local change until you tap Save changes.

q: How do I rename or move files in Q-Drive?
a: Open a file's menu (right-click on a computer, or the ⋮ button) and pick Rename or Move. To move several, select them first (on a phone, a long press selects) and use Move in the selection bar; on a computer you can also drag them onto a folder. Moving and renaming are local changes until you tap Save changes.

q: How do I share a file with one person in Q-Drive?
a:
1. Select one or more files and choose Share with a person.
2. Type their registered name and add a note if you like.
3. Confirm in Hub. It costs 0.02 QORT (0.01 for the share and 0.01 for your file list), or 0.03 if you also send a Q-Mail.
The share shows in their Shared with me, and only they can open it. They get the keys to those files only, never the rest of your drive.

q: What is a private link share in Q-Drive?
a: With Private link only, nothing on QDN points to the person: Q-Drive gives you a link (it looks like qortal://APP/Q-Drive/s/…) and you send it to them yourself. Only that person can open it. A normal share shows in their Shared with me, but anyone can work out from public data whom it is for; the link-only way hides that, unless you announce it with a Q-Mail.

q: Can I stop sharing a file in Q-Drive?
a: Yes: open Shared, then By me, and tap Stop sharing on the share (it costs a small publish fee and Hub asks you to confirm). After that, nobody can open that share in Q-Drive. It can't take back what they already got: if they opened it, they may have saved the files, and the file keys they received still open them.

q: Where do I find files someone shared with me in Q-Drive?
a: Open Shared, then With me. Files people share with you show up there; a link someone sent you can be pasted into "Open a Q-Drive link". From a share you can open or Download a file, or tap Save to my drive to keep an encrypted copy in your own drive. You don't need a drive of your own just to see what was shared with you.

q: How do I send a file by Q-Mail from Q-Drive?
a: Open the file's menu and choose Send with Q-Mail, then type their name. You can send a Secure Q-Drive link (any size; they open the files in Q-Drive, and you can stop sharing later) or attach the file itself (one file, up to 40 MB, which can't be taken back). Q-Mail shows publicly that you sent that person a mail, but not what's in it.

q: How do I publish a public copy to Q-Share from Q-Drive?
a: Open the file's menu and choose Publish a public copy to Q-Share, then give it a title, a short description and a category. Q-Share takes one file at a time from Q-Drive. Publishing makes a public copy that anyone can open on QDN, forever; the file in your drive stays private. Your public copies are listed on the Public page.

q: Can I unpublish a file I put on Q-Share from Q-Drive?
a: Yes, on the Public page tap Unpublish on that copy. Q-Share then stops listing it. The public file itself stays on QDN, and anyone who already saved a copy keeps it, so only publish copies you are happy to be public for good.

q: What is the vault passphrase in Q-Drive?
a: It is optional extra protection for your drive key, set in Settings under Security (or when you create the drive). Without it, any other app running in Hub could ask Hub to unlock your drive key without asking you; with it, they can't unless they guess the passphrase. You type it each time you unlock. Set it early: one added later can't take back a key an app already read.

q: What happens if I forget my Q-Drive vault passphrase?
a: Then nobody can open your drive: not you, not Qortal, not anyone. There is no reset. Q-Drive asks you to tick "I understand that a lost passphrase means a lost drive" before it sets one, so write it down somewhere safe and offline. A hint is optional, but other apps in Hub could read it, so never put the passphrase itself in the hint.

q: What does Lock now do in Q-Drive?
a: Lock now makes Q-Drive forget your drive key, your file list and every decrypted file from memory, and it locks Notes too. Q-Drive also locks itself when idle: Settings, Security, Auto-lock offers after 15 minutes, 1 hour (the default), 4 hours or never. Locking protects you from a harmful app opened later; with a vault passphrase you type it again to unlock.

q: Who can see my files in Q-Drive?
aliases: can people see my q-drive files
a: Anyone on QDN can see that your name uses Q-Drive, how many encrypted files and shares it stores, how big each file is and when they were published. They can't see file contents, names, types, folders or notes. People you share with see only the files you gave them, and Q-Share copies are public for good. Settings, Security, "Who can see what" lists it all.

q: Can other Q-Apps read my Q-Drive files?
a: Without a vault passphrase, an app could ask Hub to unlock your drive key without asking you. With one, it can still read your passphrase hint, shares sent to you and your Q-Mails, and could try to guess a weak passphrase. While your drive is unlocked, a harmful app open at the same time might reach Q-Drive's page, so lock Q-Drive before you open apps you don't trust.

q: Does deleting a file in Q-Drive remove it from QDN?
a: No. Move to Trash keeps the item restorable until you Delete forever or Empty trash, then Save changes. Deleting only removes it from your drive: the encrypted data stays on QDN, anyone you shared it with still has its key, and copies on Q-Share or sent with Q-Mail stay where they are. Nobody else can read the encrypted data without a key.

q: Which files can Q-Drive preview?
a: Q-Drive previews images, video, audio, PDFs, text, code, Markdown, spreadsheets, Word files and ZIP archives inside the app. Web pages are shown without scripts, forms or outside pictures. Very large files may show only their start; download them to open with another app. A damaged or crafted file from someone else could make the page stop responding, so Q-Drive warns before previewing shared files.

q: How big can a file be in Q-Drive?
a: Hub publishes files up to 2000 MB each. On a public node the limit is 500 MB per file, and some older Hub versions take only 200 MB from apps; Q-Drive tells you which limit applies. Q-Mail attachments are limited to 40 MB, so for bigger files send a Secure Q-Drive link instead.

q: Why does Q-Drive warn me that I'm on a public node?
a: A public node keeps what you publish only for a while. Unless a node of your own reads your files and your file list soon, they can disappear for good. To keep them, use Q-Drive in Hub with your own node, or have your own node follow your name so it fetches and keeps what you publish. "Got it" hides the warning until Q-Drive starts again.

q: Can I use Q-Drive on my phone with Qortal GO?
a: Yes. In Qortal GO, Q-Drive has a bottom bar (Drive, Recent, Shared, Notes, More, with Starred under More), a + button for Publish files and New folder, and a ⋮ button on each file that opens its actions in a bottom sheet; a long press selects files. If GO uses a public node, what you publish can disappear unless a node of your own reads it soon.

q: What does Find missing files do in Q-Drive?
a: It is in Settings, under Storage. Q-Drive looks on QDN for encrypted files of yours that your drive doesn't list, and you can add them back one by one or with Add all. Found files go back into the folder they were published to, or into My Drive, as a change you save. Files you deleted forever are marked "Deleted earlier" and left out unless you ask to see them.

q: What if Q-Drive says my file list can't be found?
aliases: q-drive file list can't be found
a: Tap Try again first: the list may still be on its way. If it stays gone, Restore from this device brings back the copy this device kept, with its folders. Open without it starts from an empty list and looks for your files on QDN, without folders, notes, stars or Q-Share links. Nothing is published until you tap Save, and saving replaces the lost list for good.

q: Why does Q-Drive say Waiting for your node?
a: Your node is still syncing or still fetching your drive from peers. Q-Drive checks for up to 2 minutes ("Checking your node…"), and while it waits it won't publish anything, so your files are safe. Try again shortly; if it keeps happening, make sure your node is running, synced and has connections.

q: Does each of my names get its own Q-Drive?
a: Yes. Each of your registered names has its own drive, and switching the name in the account menu opens the drive of the name you pick. Q-Drive opens on your primary name and lists your names that already have a drive first.

q: Can I use the same Q-Drive on two devices?
a: Yes, sign in with the same account on both. Your file list lives on QDN, so changes saved on one device show on the other. If both save at about the same time, Q-Drive merges them and says so; check recent renames, moves and folders, and use Find missing files in Settings if a file is missing. Each device also keeps a copy of your file list as a backup.

q: How do I download a file from Q-Drive?
a: Open the file's menu and choose Download, or select several and use Download (they go one at a time). Q-Drive fetches the encrypted file from QDN, decrypts it on your device and saves it; for a very big file it asks first. If it shows "Fetching from peers…", your node is still getting the data.

q: How do I save a shared file into my own Q-Drive?
a: Open the share in Shared, With me, and tap Save to my drive. The files go into My Drive, encrypted like the rest of your files, and Hub can approve them all at once. You need your own drive first; without one Q-Drive says "Create your drive first to save files to it."

q: What are Recent, Starred and Public in Q-Drive?
a: Recent shows the files you added or changed. Starred holds the files you starred from their menu, so you find them fast. Public lists the files you published as public copies to Q-Share, with Copy link and Unpublish. They are views of the same drive, not separate storage.

q: How do I search my files in Q-Drive?
a: Type part of a file or folder name in the search field at the top (on a phone, tap the search icon). Results come from your decrypted file list on your device, so nothing about the search is published. The search text is forgotten when the drive locks.

q: What is the Notes tab in Q-Drive?
a: Notes (in Q-Drive 1.1 and later) is a tab for plain-text notes and to-do lists. They are encrypted on your device and saved to QDN under your name when you tap Save (0.01 QORT). You can colour, pin, archive and search notes, add due dates and timers, and set an optional Notes passphrase. Notes works even if you never create a drive; open it from the Notes tab or with qortal://APP/Q-Drive/notes.

q: How do I make a note or a to-do list in Q-Drive?
a:
1. Open the Notes tab.
2. Choose New (on a phone, the + button), then New note or New list.
3. For a list, type a title, then items: Enter adds the next item, and ticked items move under Done.
4. Tap Done to close, then Save when you want it on QDN.
In the editor, Show checkboxes turns a note's lines into list items, and Hide checkboxes turns them back.

q: How do I save my notes in Q-Drive?
a: When you have changes, a bar shows how many notes changed and a Save (0.01 QORT) button. Tap it and confirm in Hub: that publishes your encrypted notes once. Nothing is saved to QDN without that tap. Until then your changes are kept on this device as a convenience, not as storage, so save before you switch devices or clear site data.

q: Can I use Q-Drive Notes without a registered name?
aliases: notes stay on this device q-drive
a: Yes, but then your notes stay on this device, for the node you use now only. Switching to another node shows none of them, and clearing site data removes them. There is also no Notes passphrase for them. Register a name in Hub (1.25 QORT) to save them to QDN; Notes then offers to add the notes you wrote before you had a name.

q: Do Q-Drive Notes timers and due dates send reminders?
a: No alerts reach you when Q-Drive is closed. A timer (1 minute up to 24 hours) rings only while Q-Drive is open on that device, and timers don't sync to your other devices. Due dates sync with your notes and show as chips such as "Due today" or "Overdue", but Q-Drive doesn't send reminders for them.

q: What is the Notes passphrase in Q-Drive?
a: It is an optional passphrase just for your notes, separate from your vault passphrase. With it, other apps in Hub need the passphrase to open your notes; without it, any app you open can ask Hub to open them without asking you. Add, change or remove it in Notes settings (each is a save, 0.01 QORT). If you lose it, nobody can open those notes; there is no reset.

q: I forgot my Q-Drive Notes passphrase. What can I do?
a: Without the passphrase the locked notes can't be opened by anyone. On the lock screen, "Forgot it?" leads to Start over: that publishes empty notes in their place, and the old ones are gone for good. Only do this when you are sure the passphrase is lost.

q: How do I hide the Notes tab in Q-Drive?
a: Go to Settings, Tabs, and turn off "Show the Notes tab". It is free and instant, and it only applies to that device. Turning it off hides the tab and stops Notes reading anything. If you have unsaved notes, Q-Drive asks first and says whether they stay on the device.

q: Can I colour, pin or archive notes in Q-Drive?
a: Yes. Each note card's menu has Pin, Colour (no colour, yellow, green, blue, pink, purple, orange or grey), Due date, Timer, Move up, down, to top or to bottom, Archive and Move to trash. Pinned notes show first. In the Trash tab you can Restore a note or Delete forever; deleting can't take back what other apps or devices already read.

q: What happens if I edit Q-Drive notes on two devices?
a: Notes merges saves note by note. When the same text changed on both devices, it keeps both versions as copies so nothing is lost, and when a save replaced one from another device it offers you a review. Save on one device and wait for it to arrive before editing on the other to keep things simple.

q: How many notes can Q-Drive Notes hold?
aliases: how long can a note be q-drive
a: This version handles up to 2,000 notes. A note can be up to 20,000 characters (a counter appears near the end), and a list up to 200 items. Anyone on QDN can see roughly how much you keep, in 4 KB steps, but not what your notes say.

q: Does Lock now in Q-Drive also lock my notes?
aliases: q-drive notes locked after a while
a: Yes. Lock now in the menu, More or Settings locks both the drive and Notes. Notes also has its own "Lock notes now" and "Lock notes automatically" (after 15 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours or never) in Notes settings. If changes can't be kept on the device, Q-Drive asks before locking.

q: How do I open Qortal Web Builder?
a: Qortal Web Builder is published as the Q-App QWB. Open it from the Apps list in Qortal Hub, or with qortal://APP/QWB. It needs Hub (or GO) to sign you in and publish, so opening its files in a normal web browser won't let you connect.

q: What do I need to build a website with QWB?
a: A Qortal account and a registered name, plus a little QORT for publish fees. When QWB opens, Step 1 is "Connect wallet (authenticate)" so it knows your account, and Step 2 asks which registered name the site belongs to. Your website is published under that name as qortal://WEBSITE/<your name>.

q: How do I build a website in Qortal Web Builder?

a:
1. Open QWB, authenticate and pick your registered name.
2. In Add blocks, click a block type (header, hero, text, photos, shop and more) to add it at the end.
3. Select a block to move or edit it in the Options sidebar on the right, where you also manage pages; the site theme is in Settings.
4. Tap Save as Draft to keep your work on QDN.
5. Tap Publish Website when it is ready.
No coding is needed; you can check the phone layout with Mobile View.

q: How do I publish my website from QWB?

QWB builds your site bundle and sends it, with the forum, poll and index files it needs, to Hub as one batch, showing how many transactions it holds before you approve. A progress window follows each step, then says "Your website is live at" your qortal://WEBSITE/<name> link and opens it in a new Hub tab. Each publish has the usual small QDN fee.

q: How do I save a draft in Qortal Web Builder?

The button turns to Draft saved when the copy on QDN matches your current site. Load saved draft overwrites the working page with that last saved draft.

q: What blocks can I add in Qortal Web Builder?

q: Can visitors comment or vote on my QWB website?

q: Can I make a QWB website only for my group?

q: How do I use another website as a template in QWB?

q: Can I embed Q-Apps in my Qortal Web Builder site?

q: How do I see my QWB website on a phone screen?
a: Tap Mobile View in the top bar to preview the site inside a phone-sized frame, and tap it again to go back to the normal editor width. Published sites adapt to phones: a header with more than three buttons folds into a menu button, and blocks stack for small screens.

q: How do I add pages to my QWB website?
a: Pages are managed in the Options sidebar on the right of the builder; if the panel is folded, open it with the tab on the right edge of the screen. From there you can add, open, rename, copy the link to, or remove pages. The Header block's buttons give visitors the navigation between them.

q: Can I export or back up my QWB website?
a: Yes. In Settings, Export website .zip builds the same bundle as Publish Website and saves it to your device. Import a website .zip loads such a file back, so you can edit it and publish again. Save as Draft also keeps a copy on QDN.

q: Can I have more than one website project in QWB?
a: Yes. In Settings, Project, + New project adds another saved workspace in this browser, with its own site draft, and you can switch between them. A project doesn't create a new registered name: a website is published under a registered name, so a second live site needs a second name, picked with the name switcher in the top bar.

q: Can I add a newsletter or contact form to my QWB site?
a: Yes. The Newsletter block keeps a Q-Mail subscriber list and lets you send campaigns, and the Contact form block sends visitors' messages to you as encrypted Q-Mail. Both use Qortal accounts, so visitors authenticate before they subscribe or write.

q: How do I put music or videos on my QWB website?
a: Use the Video block to upload a video or embed one from Q-Tube, and the Music block for albums with an on-page player, synced with Q-Music. The Folders block is a file library that can publish to Q-Share, Q-Tube and Q-Music, with image, audio and PDF viewers for visitors.

q: How do I change the Built with Qortal Web Builder footer?

q: Why does my QWB website show the starter template or fail to load?
a: Sites published with older QWB versions could load the starter template instead of their content when the site was large. Open the site in the current QWB and tap Publish Website again: since 1.0.0 the site's settings ship as their own file. If a visitor sees "This website could not load its configuration", the fix is the same: republish from Qortal Web Builder.

q: Why do visitors need to Authenticate on a QWB website?
a: Anyone can browse a QWB site, but posting, voting, checkout and other wallet actions need the visitor's account, so the site asks them to tap Authenticate first. It is never automatic. Authenticate only works when the site is opened inside Qortal Hub or GO (for example from qortal://WEBSITE/<name>), not in an ordinary web browser.

q: What is the Qortal Web Q-App?
a: Qortal Web is a Q-App that searches and lists everything published with Qortal Web Builder: websites, forums, polls, articles, videos, music, photos, folders and shops. It reads the small index files QWB publishes beside each site, so you can search by title or browse by kind, then open the site or a single block right there. Open it from Apps or with qortal://APP/Qortal Web.

q: How do I find websites made with Qortal Web Builder?
a: Open the Qortal Web Q-App (qortal://APP/Qortal Web). Its home page shows network stats, top publishers and Discover websites cards; you can search, or browse by category such as websites, forums, articles, video, music or folders. Tap a result to see it in place, or Visit website to open the full site in Hub.

q: How does my QWB website get listed on Qortal Web?

qortal web not showing my site
a: When you tap Publish Website in QWB, it also publishes a small index file listing your site and its forums, polls, articles, media and folders. Qortal Web reads those files, so a Global site shows up there after the network has seen your publish. A group-only site is shown only to signed-in members of that group.

q: What is the Q-Shops marketplace?
a: Q-Shops is a marketplace Q-App that gathers the Q-Shop storefronts built with Qortal Web Builder into one directory. You can browse many shops and their products, put items from several shops in one cart, pay each shop through Hub, and keep your orders and invoices in one place. Open it from Apps or with qortal://APP/Q-Shops.

q: How do I buy something in the Q-Shops marketplace?
a:
1. Open Q-Shops and browse Products or Shops; add items to the Cart.
2. Tap Authenticate in the header, then Checkout.
3. Choose Ship / deliver, Pickup, or nothing for a digital-only cart, and fill in your details.
4. Tap Pay this shop and approve the payment in Hub.
The seller gets a Q-Mail about the order and you get a receipt. A payment you approved can't be undone.

q: How do I get my shop listed on Q-Shops?
a: Build your store with the Q-Shop block in Qortal Web Builder and publish your website. QWB publishes the shop's catalog to QDN, and Q-Shops finds those catalogs by searching QDN and merges them into its directory, refreshing now and then. There is no separate sign-up.

q: Where are my orders in Q-Shops?
a: Tap My orders in the toolbar (it shows a count). Your orders and invoices are kept for your wallet; open one to see the invoice, save it as PDF, or download digital items again. My orders needs you to authenticate, and orders are saved in that browser or app, so they won't show on another device.

q: What if Q-Shops says my payment went through but the seller wasn't told?
a: Paying and notifying the seller are two steps. If the payment succeeded but the order Q-Mail failed, Q-Shops says so; your payment was still sent, so don't pay again. Check the payment in your Hub wallet activity, and contact the seller with the order details. An invoice that says "Paid, verify in Hub" means Hub returned no transaction reference.

q: Can I sell with a Q-Asset instead of QORT in a QWB shop?
a: Yes. The Q-Shop checkout lets the buyer pay in QORT or in a custom Q-Asset you choose, and the transfer goes through Hub, where the buyer approves it. Buyers who find your shop in the Q-Shops app can pay the same ways.

q: What is Subscreen?
a: Subscreen is a Q-App for movies and TV series from the Qortal community, all in one place. You can find something to watch, rate titles, help add the cast and crew, bookmark titles and publish your own. It uses Q-Tube's format, so what you publish on Subscreen also appears on Q-Tube, and Q-Tube movies and series show in Subscreen.

q: How do I open Subscreen?
a: Open Subscreen from the Apps list in Qortal Hub or Qortal GO, or with qortal://APP/Subscreen. Watching works for everyone; tap Sign in and approve the request in Hub when you want to rate, comment, bookmark to QDN or publish.

q: Do I need a registered name to use Subscreen?
a: Not to watch. To rate, comment and publish you need a registered name: Subscreen says to register one in Qortal Hub (1.25 QORT). If you have several names, comments, ratings and publishes use the name you select in the account menu.

q: How do I watch a movie on Subscreen?
a: Pick a title from Home, Movies or Series, or use Search, and press Play on its page. A title new to your node shows "Fetching from peers…" while your node gathers the video, which can take a moment. On phones one tap shows the player buttons without pausing, and in fullscreen you swipe up or down on the left for brightness and on the right for volume.

q: How do I find a movie or series on Subscreen?
a: Use Search to find a film or series by title, an actor or director, or a Qortal publisher. In Movies or Series, Filters narrow by genre, year (including ranges such as 2020 and newer), quality and length (under 90 or over 150 minutes), with sorting too. Genres and years on a title page are links to matching titles.

q: How do I rate a title on Subscreen?
a: Sign in with a registered name, open the title and pick a score from 1 to 10 under Your rating. Subscreen publishes it to QDN under your name, so confirm in Qortal Hub if asked; others see it after a minute or two. When you finish a title it asks "How was it?". You can change your score later or tap Clear to withdraw it.

q: How do I comment on a title in Subscreen?
a: Sign in and write in Comments on the title page, up to 200 characters, then confirm in Hub. Subscreen uses the same thread as Q-Tube, so comments posted here also appear there, and Q-Tube comments show here.

q: How do I tip a publisher on Subscreen?
a: After you rate a title 6 or higher, Subscreen offers to thank its publisher with a tip in QORT, with an optional comment. Hub asks you to confirm twice: once for the tip and once to show it on the title page (0.01 QORT), where a comment is highlighted in gold. Tips can't be undone, so check the amount before you confirm.

q: How do I bookmark titles on Subscreen?
a: Tap the bookmark button on a title to pin it to Watch Later or to one of your own lists (up to 20 lists). Bookmarks (the Saved tab on phones) shows them all, where you can rename or delete lists. When you are signed in, lists are stored on QDN for your Qortal name, so they come back on another device; if a save to QDN didn't go through, they are kept on the device and Bookmarks offers Save to QDN.

q: Where is my watch history in Subscreen?
a: Home shows Continue watching and Recently watched, and History lists everything you pressed Play on, even if the video was still fetching. History is kept on that device only, not published, and Clear history removes it.

q: How do I download a movie from Subscreen?
a: Tap Download on the title page. The video is copied to your Qortal node first, then saved to your device; confirm the save if Qortal asks. If your node doesn't have it yet, Subscreen shows the fetch from QDN before saving. A large video takes a moment to copy.

q: Does Subscreen have subtitles?
a: Yes, when someone has published them. Pick a track in the player's subtitle menu. Signed in with a registered name, you can add SRT or VTT files up to 2 MB with "Add or edit subtitles"; the language is guessed from names like movie.en.srt, and each track is published under your name. Subtitles use Q-Tube's format, so they show in both apps.

q: What are Cast and Crew on Subscreen?
a: Cast & Crew lists the people credited on titles, each with a page of their titles. Anyone signed in can help: on a title, use Add cast & crew, pick a role and search for a person or type a new name. Each credit publishes a small update under your name (about 0.01 QORT, Hub asks to confirm). You can edit or remove credits you added, and the title's publisher can change any.

q: How do I publish a movie on Subscreen?
a:
1. Sign in with a registered name and tap Publish.
2. Drop your movie file first: the title, year, length and quality fill in from it.
3. Add a vertical 2:3 poster (recommended), genre, description, and optionally a trailer and cast & crew.
4. Check the summary and confirm in Qortal Hub.
It is published in Q-Tube's format under your name, so it appears on both Subscreen and Q-Tube. The fee is 0.01 QORT per resource: a movie is two, plus one each for a trailer and cast & crew.

q: How do I publish a TV series on Subscreen?
a: On Publish, choose a series and add every episode at once: they publish together as one series. The series title and episode numbers fill in from the file names, and names like S01E02 set the season and episode. Sort by episode to check the order before you publish. For a show with several seasons that is already published, bundle one season at a time under the same name.

q: Which video format works best on Subscreen?
a: MP4 with AV1 video and Opus sound works best. Subscreen warns before publishing when a file won't play in Hub, such as MKV or H.265 (HEVC) video, or would play without sound, such as Dolby Digital (AC-3) audio. Convert such files first so everyone can watch them.

q: How big a video can I publish on Subscreen?
a: Qortal Hub publishes files up to 2 GB. On a public node the limit is 500 MB per file, so use smaller files or publish with your own node. Your node's drive also needs room for the file, and big files take a long time to publish: keep Subscreen open until Hub finishes.

q: Why does Subscreen say a title is already on Subscreen?
a: Before you publish, Subscreen checks whether the same movie or series is already there and compares your copy's quality with the best one. You can still publish yours, in better quality or as another version. Copies of the same movie are combined into one card, with a choice of versions on its page.

q: How do I edit or replace my video on Subscreen?
a: Open My publishes (or the title) and tap Edit. You can change the details, poster and trailer, or use Replace video file. The title keeps its link, comments, ratings and cast & crew, and the new file takes the old one's place. Publishing a new file is two Hub confirmations: the file, then its details.

q: Can I remove a title I published on Subscreen?
a: Yes: Edit, then Remove from Subscreen. That also hides it in Q-Tube. QDN has no real delete, though: copies may still exist on other nodes and the video file stays published, and ratings, comments and cast & crew are not removed.

q: What are collections on Subscreen?
a: A publisher can group movies they already published, such as a franchise or a comedian's specials, into a collection; each movie's page then shows the rest. On My publishes, Bundle into a series or collection does this, and the same tool bundles separately published videos into a series. The videos aren't published again.

q: How do I hide genres or publishers on Subscreen?
a: Use Don't show in the catalog toolbar and pick the genres or publishers you'd rather not see in lists and search. It only changes what you see, on this device. Publishers label their own videos, so some may still get through.

q: Why won't a video play on Subscreen?
a: Usually your node is still getting the video from peers: wait and try again in a moment. If Subscreen says there is no playable video on QDN yet, the publisher hasn't published the video file, so ask them to. Files in formats Hub can't play, such as MKV or H.265, may also fail; MP4 with AV1 and Opus works best.

q: What can I do with POS+ on Qortal?
a: POS+ is a point-of-sale Q-App for shops, market stalls and pop-up sellers, running inside Qortal Hub and Qortal GO. You ring up sales paid by card, cash or both, give discounts and refunds, show and save receipts, clock staff in and out, run several locations, and see sales and VAT with exportable reports. Products, receipts and daily sales are tied to your registered name and stored on QDN, mostly encrypted, with no server or subscription. Open it from the Apps list by searching POS+.

q: How do I set up my store in POS+?
a:
1. Open POS+ and tap Connect wallet, then approve the request in Hub or GO.
2. Choose Business owner.
3. Pick one of your registered names as the store (tap a name chip).
4. Leave "Keep me signed in on this device" ticked and tap Continue to POS+.
5. Add products, and fill in Settings (company, receipt, locations, VAT and currency), then tap Save to QDN.
After that, POS+ opens your store automatically on that device.

q: How do staff sign in to POS+?
a: The owner first adds the staff member's registered name under Settings, Sales Force, and saves. The staff member then opens POS+, connects their wallet, chooses Staff, types the business's registered name and picks their location. Staff get the Sell, Today and Settings tabs and only see and change their own sales.

q: How do I add products in POS+?
a: In the Products tab, use New product: enter a name and a price with VAT included, pick the VAT rate, and tap Add. Add or change the photo on the product's card afterwards, edit names and prices on each card, and reorder with the up and down arrows (the Sell grid follows that order). Tap Save changes to publish everything to QDN in one approval.

q: How do I ring up a sale in POS+?
a: In the Sell tab, tap products to add them to the cart; quick catalog tabs help you find items faster. A bar appears with Card, Cash, Review and Cancel. For a normal sale at shelf price, tap Card or Cash and you are done. Use Review when you need a different price, a discount, a split payment or a note on the receipt.

q: How do I give a discount in POS+?
a: Tap Review instead of Card or Cash. There you can change the unit price of any line, or set an order discount of None, 5%, 10% or Other % (type it and tap Apply). Once a discount is set, untick a line to keep that product at full price. Then take the payment, and the receipt opens.

q: How do I split a payment between cash and card in POS+?
a: Tap Review, choose split payment, and type one of the amounts, cash or card; POS+ fills in the other automatically. Then finish the payment and the receipt shows both parts.

q: How do I refund a sale in POS+?
a: Open the Today tab and find the sale. Refund records a full or partial refund with an optional note; it shows on the receipt and counts in all totals. If a sale was entered by mistake, Remove deletes it (POS+ asks first). You can also correct the invoice total or add a note there.

q: How do I show or save a receipt in POS+?
a: In the Today tab, tap Receipt on a sale. Full screen shows it large, opened in Hub's or GO's own PDF viewer, which is handy to show a customer. Save PDF saves it to your device as a receipt-sized PDF that looks like a printed receipt, with your logo.

q: How do I close the day in POS+?
a: At the end of the day, open Today and tap "Publish today to QDN & clear draft", then approve in Hub. It publishes this device's sales for its location, encrypted for you and your Sales Force, clears the device's draft for tomorrow, and clocks out anyone still on shift on that device. Until a day is closed its sales exist only on that device, so close the day on every device that sold something.

q: Why are sales missing from POS+ Stats?
a: Stats only shows closed days. Make sure the day was closed with "Publish today to QDN & clear draft" on every device that sold something, including staff devices, then tap Refresh from QDN. If it says data is unavailable, your node is still fetching from peers; POS+ waits and retries on its own.

q: How do I see my sales reports in POS+?
a: Open Stats (owner only). Pick a preset such as Today, This month or Last year, set your own From and To dates, or tap and drag days on the calendar, which marks days with sales. Filter by location and worker. You see the total with the card and cash split, a VAT table per rate, a product summary, and each day's sales with their receipts.

q: How do I export my sales from POS+?
a: In Stats, pick the period, then Export CSV for totals, the VAT table and the product summary, ready for a spreadsheet or your accountant. Export PDF makes a report with your logo: totals, VAT summary, items summary, location summary and the full sales log. In Hub and GO it is saved as a file you can open, print or keep.

q: How do staff clock in and out in POS+?
a: Tap Clock in in the top bar to open Shifts, then Clock in or Clock out with one tap. While on shift the top bar shows On shift and the time worked; clocking out works after midnight or from another device. Each clock-in is shared live with the owner as a small encrypted publish that Hub asks you to approve. If it wasn't shared, your hours are still on the device: tap Share again.

q: How does the owner see who is working in POS+?
a: In Shifts, the owner sees Live now: who is clocked in right now, across all locations and devices, and can clock someone out from there. Work hours shows hours per team member for any date range, and Edit corrects a shift's times, for example when someone forgot to clock out, with a note.

q: How do I add staff to my POS+ store?
a: Go to Settings, Sales Force, add each person by their registered Qortal name, and tap Save to QDN. Staff must own their name. Removing someone later stops them reading anything saved after that. Staff publish their day-closes and clock-ins under their own names, and your Stats picks them up.

q: Why can't my staff see any products in POS+?
aliases: pos+ products not showing for staff
a: The owner opens Settings, Sales Force and taps "Re-share store with team". The product list is encrypted for the owner and the Sales Force, so a staff member added later needs the store shared with them again before they can read it.

q: How do I set up several locations in POS+?
a: In Settings, Receipt seller & locations, add as many locations as you need, such as a main shop or a market stall, and choose the default for new devices. On each device, set Settings, This device, Location of this device. Each location closes its own sales day, and renaming a location keeps its history.
source: ~/Desktop/POS/POS+ user guide (Subwire).md §8 (Receipt seller & locations, This device)

q: How do I set VAT and currency in POS+?
a: In Settings, Tax & currency, set the default VAT % for new products, the VAT rates to choose from, the currency code and how many decimals prices show (0 to 3, or per currency, such as USD:2 or ISK:0). Prices in POS+ include VAT; each product's own rate is used for the receipt breakdown and the Stats VAT table.

q: How do I put my logo and company details on POS+ receipts?
a: In Settings, Company & receipt, fill in the display and legal name, address, phone, email, company ID and VAT number, a receipt footer such as a thank-you or return policy, and the store logo (PNG, JPG or SVG). Then tap Save to QDN. The logo shows in the top bar, on receipts and on reports, and it is public on QDN.

q: Is my POS+ sales data private?
a: Mostly. The product list, the staff list, shift records and closed sales days are encrypted on QDN, readable only by you and the staff you add. Product photos, the store logo and basic store information (the owner's Qortal address, location names and currency) are public, so don't put anything private in a photo. Sales not yet published stay on the device until you close the day.

q: How do I import past sales into POS+?
a: In Settings, Moderation, use Publish Past Sales to import historical sales from one or more CSV files, split by location if needed. Clear published days lets you remove chosen days from Stats so you can import them again.

q: How do I reset my POS+ sales and stats?
a: In Settings, Moderation, Reset Sales and Stats starts Stats from zero. Unpublished drafts are first saved as a CSV backup, and staff, locations, products and settings are kept. Think before you use it: the old stats are no longer shown afterwards.

q: How do I switch to another store in POS+?
a: Tap the ⇄ button in the top bar, or go to Settings, Switch store. If Hub is signed in to a different account, POS+ asks you to choose the store. The Dark and Light theme toggle sits next to the POS+ title.

q: Why does POS+ say Data unavailable or load slowly?
a: Your node is still fetching the store's data from peers. POS+ waits and retries on its own, and in the meantime it opens with the copy saved on the device, so you can keep selling while QDN is slow. Product photos load after the store opens.

q: How do quick catalogs work in POS+?
a: Quick catalogs are your own tabs on the Sell screen, such as Drinks, Lunch or Seasonal. In Products, tap + Catalog, give it a name, choose its products (search, Select all and Clear all help), and tap Save tab. Then tap Save changes on Products to publish it to QDN. All always shows every product.

q: What is the World Map Q-App?
a: World Map is a map Q-App for sharing places. It shows map tiles stored on QDN with country, road and place overlays, and lets you save points of interest (POIs) and lists of places, browse everyone's public POIs, and post to a World Feed with photos, videos and locations. It can also show pins from ThankQ and Freedom Cells. Open it from Apps or with qortal://APP/World Map.
source: ~/Desktop/World Map/q-app/index.html, QDN APP World Map metadata

q: How do I add a place to World Map?
a:
1. Sign in with a registered name and tap + Add POI.
2. Give it a title and region, then set the coordinates: tap "Set from map" and tap once on the map, or drag the red pin.
3. Add a description, tags, up to 6 photos and the lists it belongs to.
4. Choose Public or Private and tap Save to QDN, then confirm in Hub.
If a photo carries GPS coordinates, World Map offers to use them for the pin.

q: Are private places on World Map really private?
a: A Private POI or list is encrypted when your Hub supports it. If encryption isn't available, World Map warns "Encryption unavailable, stored as private JSON (not encrypted)", which means it is only hidden from the app's lists, not secret. Public POIs and lists are visible to everyone, so never pin your home or other private spots publicly.

q: How do I make a list of places on World Map?
a: Open My Lists and tap + New list, give it a name and description, pick Public or Private, add POIs and tap Save list. You can also pick lists when you save a POI. Public lists appear in Discover, where others can view and recommend them.

q: What is Discover on World Map?
a: Discover lists everyone's public POIs and lists, sorted by community score. The score is the average star rating times ln(2 + number of ratings); POIs also gain 0.02 per view, and anything gains 2.5 per community recommendation. Hover over or long-press a score to see how it was worked out, and use Recommend to support a place or list.

q: What is the World Feed on World Map?
a: World Feed shows the newest POIs and posts from the network, with All, Posts, POI's and Mine filters. To post, write up to 4,000 characters and add a photo, a video or a tagged location, then Post to Feed. Posts are published to QDN under your Qortal name and visible to everyone. Videos are published to Q-Tube after you fill in their details, so they also show there.

q: How do I search the World Map?
a: Type a place name, a #tag, or coordinates into Search. A place or coordinates moves the map there; a tag shows the POIs tagged with it. If nothing matches, World Map says to try a place, #tag or coordinates.

q: How do I see ThankQ hosts on World Map?
a: Under Q-App integrations, tap + ThankQ (or + Freedom Cells). World Map loads that app's pins with coordinates from QDN and adds them as a layer; tap its chip to show or hide the pins, or × to remove it.

q: Why does the World Map look plain or show no map pictures?
a: The map pictures (tiles) come from QDN, and your node fetches them from peers. Where a tile isn't available yet, World Map falls back to its simple outline map, so the map still works. Zoom in on an area or wait a moment, and the detailed tiles load as your node gets them.

q: What is ThankQ?
a: ThankQ is a hospitality Q-App where people on Qortal host each other, organise meetups and build trust, with no middleman. You can offer a place to stay, post that you are open to meet for coffee or a walk, share that you are travelling to an event, or lend tools and gear. Open it from Apps or with qortal://APP/ThankQ, and tap Authenticate with an account that has a registered name.

q: Do I need a registered name to use ThankQ?
a: Yes. ThankQ opens on a welcome screen with an Authenticate button, and it shows listings, requests and your profile only after you connect an account that has a registered name. Without one it says you need a registered Qortal name and to register one first, in Hub or GO.

q: How do I offer a place to stay on ThankQ?
a: Tap + Hosting (or Add, then Create Hosting). Fill in the title, city, country, description, maximum guests, availability (Available, Full or Hidden), tags and up to 6 photos, then Publish and confirm in Hub. Coordinates are optional, but add them for an exact pin: with them blank, ThankQ tries to place the pin from the city and country, and asks you to add coordinates when it can't.

q: How do I post a meetup on ThankQ?
a: Tap + Meetup. Add a title, your city and country, a few words about you, and what you are open to: coffee, walk, chat, dinner, local tour, hike, co-work, events or a Qortal popup. Set your status (Active or Away) and an availability note, then Post Meetup. Others can then tap Suggest a Meetup to reach you.

q: How do I share an event trip on ThankQ?
a: Tap + Event to post that you are travelling to an event: the event name, city, country, venue and the start and end dates, with optional photos. Others going there can connect with you. Past events are hidden unless you tick See past events.

q: How do I lend or borrow tools on ThankQ?
a: In the Borrow tab, tap + Borrow to offer a tool: pick a category, its condition, how you lend it (free, with a QORT deposit, or negotiated), pickup or shipping, and photos. To borrow something, open it and tap Request to borrow with the dates you need and a message.

q: How do I request a stay on ThankQ?
a: Open a hosting listing and tap Request a Stay. Pick your arrival and departure dates, the number of guests and write a message to the host, then Send Request and confirm in Hub. ThankQ publishes the request and also tells the host by Q-Chat and Q-Mail. You see its status under Requests, Outgoing.

q: Can other people read my ThankQ requests?
a: Yes. ThankQ publishes listings, profiles, requests and reviews as public data on QDN under your name, so anyone can read them, including your dates and message. Don't put your home address, phone number or other private details in a listing or request; share those only once you trust the person, and in a private chat.

q: How do I accept or decline a request on ThankQ?
a: Open Requests, Incoming, and tap Accept or Decline on a pending request. To cancel a request you already accepted, use Cancel Request and give a reason, which is required. Outgoing shows the requests you sent and their status: pending, accepted, declined or cancelled.

q: How do reviews work on ThankQ?
a: After a completed stay or meetup that the host accepted, you can Leave a Review with a star rating and a few words, published to QDN. ThankQ only lets you review a host after such an accepted stay or meetup, which keeps reviews tied to real visits.

q: How do I edit my profile on ThankQ?
a: Open Profile and tap Edit My Profile. Add a bio, city, country, languages, interests and places you have lived, and up to 6 photos. Tick Open for Meetups to show you on the meetup map, pick what you are open to, then Save Profile. Your profile is public, so it helps guests and hosts know you before reaching out.

q: Can I delete a listing on ThankQ?
a: Yes: tap Remove on it and confirm. QDN data can't be erased, so ThankQ overwrites the entry with a deleted flag, and it then disappears everywhere in ThankQ. The earlier version may still exist on QDN.

q: What is Q-Weather?
a: Q-Weather is a weather forecast app for Qortal Hub and Qortal GO. For each of your places it shows a chart of the coming days (the meteogram), a list of days and a map with weather layers. Everything comes over QDN from your own node: it never contacts an outside server, needs no account and doesn't track you. Open it from Apps or with qortal://APP/Q-Weather.
source: QDN APP Q-Weather 1.0.5 (published bundle, How Q-Weather works), ~/Desktop/Q-Weather/README.md

q: Where do Q-Weather forecasts come from?
a: The base everywhere is ECMWF IFS, the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts' global model, at 9 km, up to 15 days ahead. Where a high-resolution regional model covers a place (the USA, Canada, Iceland, Poland and much of Europe), the first two to three days come from it, hour by hour. A publisher computer turns the open data into compact files and publishes them on QDN under the name Q-Weather, four runs a day.
source: QDN APP Q-Weather 1.0.5 (published bundle, How Q-Weather works), ~/Desktop/Q-Weather/README.md (howSources, howQdn, howUpdates)

q: How often does Q-Weather update?
a: ECMWF starts four runs a day, at 00, 06, 12 and 18 UTC, and each is published on QDN about 10 hours after it starts, with the newest regional runs. Q-Weather checks for new data when you open it and every 10 minutes while it is open. If your node has only an older run, it says which one it is showing.
source: QDN APP Q-Weather 1.0.5 (published bundle, How Q-Weather works), ~/Desktop/Q-Weather/README.md (howUpdates)

q: How do I add a place in Q-Weather?
a: Tap Add place and type at least 2 letters of a town or city; bigger places can be found by their names in GO's 12 languages, and you can also type coordinates. Or tap the map and choose Add this place. Q-Weather knows about 226,000 towns of 500 people or more. Your places and settings stay on your device.
source: QDN APP Q-Weather 1.0.5 (published bundle, How Q-Weather works), ~/Desktop/Q-Weather/README.md (places strings, howPlaces)

q: How do I read the Q-Weather chart?
a: Days run left to right, with each day's high (orange) and low (blue) above. Yellow is clear sky; grey bands are clouds (high at the top, low at the bottom); blue bars are rain and light blue snow; the green line is wind and the white line temperature. Orange shading means warmer than the day before, blue colder, and a violet line marks freezing. The thin red line is now: drag across the chart to move the thick red line, and the map follows.
source: QDN APP Q-Weather 1.0.5 (published bundle, How Q-Weather works), ~/Desktop/Q-Weather/README.md (guide strings)

q: What does the Q-Weather map show?
a: Open Layers to pick from 21 map layers, grouped as precipitation and clouds, temperature and sun, wind and pressure, sea, and upper air: for example rain and snow, total and low cloud, temperature, feels like, wind with moving streaks, gusts, pressure with isobars, thunderstorm energy (CAPE), waves, sea temperature, snow and the jet stream. The map shows the moment you pick in the chart and moves with it.
source: QDN APP Q-Weather 1.0.5 (published bundle, How Q-Weather works), ~/Desktop/Q-Weather/README.md (layers, howMap)

q: How do I change units or theme in Q-Weather?
a: Open the menu, then Settings. Under Appearance pick the theme (Auto, Light or Dark) and the map style (Dark, Light or Terrain). Under Units set time, temperature, precipitation, wind, pressure and height. Under Charts choose how many days the chart shows (3 to 15) and whether to shade the nights.
source: QDN APP Q-Weather 1.0.5 (published bundle, How Q-Weather works), ~/Desktop/Q-Weather/README.md (settings strings)

q: How do I add Q-Weather widgets in GO?
a: Q-Weather has three GO widgets: Weather Bars (the days ahead as bars, with rain and weather icons), Weather Chart (clouds, rain, wind and temperature as a chart) and Weather Now (the weather right now, over a matching sky). In Q-Weather, open a place's ⋮ menu and tap Show in GO widgets to choose the place they show. Then on GO's widgets screen tap + and add the ones you like; tapping a widget opens Q-Weather.
source: QDN APP Q-Weather 1.0.5 (published bundle, How Q-Weather works), ~/Desktop/Q-Weather/README.md (useInWidget, v103Widgets), QDN APP metadata of Weather Bars, Weather Chart, Weather Now

q: Why does Q-Weather say the forecast is not on my node yet?
a: Your node hasn't fetched the newest forecast files from other nodes yet; Q-Weather shows "Fetching from QDN…" with a percentage while it does. Wait a moment and try again. "Your node did not answer" means the node itself isn't reachable, and "Q-Weather data is blocked on this node" means the node blocks that name's data.
source: QDN APP Q-Weather 1.0.5 (published bundle, How Q-Weather works), ~/Desktop/Q-Weather/README.md (noForecast, notPublished, blocked, offline, stale)

q: What is the GO Clock widget?
a: GO Clock is a small clock widget for the Qortal GO widgets screen, published as the Q-App GO Clock. It shows the time with seconds and the date in your language, and follows GO's light or dark theme. Tap it to switch between 24-hour and 12-hour time; it remembers your choice. Add it from the widgets screen's + button and resize it like any widget.

q: What is the Singularity game on Qortal?
a: Singularity is a small game Q-App: you fly your Qortal avatar, mint blocks and dodge black holes before the singularity claims you. Anyone can play, even as a guest; a registered name is only needed to save a score. It has a public leaderboard of verified scores, and shows the live Qortal network height while you play. Open it from Apps or with qortal://APP/Singularity.

q: How do I play Singularity?
a: Tap Play. On a computer thrust with WASD or the arrow keys; on a phone hold and drag. Touch blocks to mint them, and dodge the drifting black hole, the mini holes and a rival ship (the next player above you on the leaderboard). You can ram rivals into holes, and outscoring them makes them flee. The black hole grows as it swallows blocks; Esc exits.

q: How do I save my score in Singularity?
a: Sign in with a registered name, beat your verified best (you must mint at least one block), then tap Save verified score and approve in Hub. Hub asks only when you save. The score is checked against your run and published to QDN, and the leaderboard shows verified gameplay scores only; forged entries are filtered out.

q: What is the GIFs Q-App?
a: GIFs is a community GIF library for Qortal chat, published as the Q-App GIFs. You can add GIFs, or a batch of files, tag them with search words, find them later and copy them into chats. GIFs added there also appear in the GIF picker of Q-Chat in Hub and GO and in Torq's composer. Open it from Apps or with qortal://APP/GIFs.

q: How do I add GIFs to the GIFs library?
a:
1. Open GIFs and go to Add.
2. Drop or choose GIF or short MP4 files, up to 20 at a time; short MP4s become GIFs, and files over 2 MB are shrunk just enough to fit.
3. Give each one at least one search word (up to 8).
4. Publish and approve the batch in Hub.
You need a registered name to add or like GIFs.

q: How do I use a GIF from the GIFs app in a chat?
a: In the GIFs app, open a GIF and tap Copy embed link, then paste it into a Qortal chat. Or stay in the chat: in Q-Chat in Hub or GO, open the emoji panel and switch it from Emojis to GIFs to search the same community library.

q: How do I edit or remove my GIFs in the GIFs app?
a: Open Mine to see the GIFs you published under your name. From there you can edit a GIF's search words or remove it from the library. Removing hides it from the library; like anything on QDN, the published file itself isn't erased.

q: Who moderates the GIFs library?
a: Only the registered name GIFs, the app's publisher, can use the Moderate tab to hide a GIF or block a name. Hidden GIFs and blocked names are left out of the library, and out of the GIFs in Q-Chat's emoji panel, which reads the same moderation list.

q: What is Q-MEME?
a: Q-MEME is a community meme app for Qortal, in the same style as the GIFs app. You can share finished memes, make a meme by putting words on a community template or on any picture of your own, and publish blank templates for others to caption. Every meme can be saved to your device or copied into a Qortal chat. Open it from Apps or with qortal://APP/Q-MEME.

q: How do I make a meme in Q-MEME?
a:
1. In Library, Templates, tap a template or its Use button. To use your own photo instead, go to Add, Meme and choose Make a meme from a picture.
2. Type your words in the text spots and adjust them.
3. Add search words and publish, approving in Hub.
GIF templates stay animated: the preview moves while you type, and the meme is published as an animated GIF.

q: How do I upload memes to Q-MEME?
a: Go to Add, Meme and upload up to 12 finished memes at once (JPG, PNG, WebP or GIF). Add search words to each (popular ones are suggested) and publish. Add text first opens the editor if you want to put words on one before publishing.

q: How do I publish a template in Q-MEME?
a: Go to Add, Template and upload blank pictures. Mark where the text goes, add search words, and publish. Your templates then show in Library, Templates for anyone to caption, and you can edit their picture, words or text spots later from Mine.

q: How do I share a meme from Q-MEME in chat?
a: Tap a meme to see it full size, then Copy for chat and paste it into a Qortal chat, or Save to keep it on your device. In GO, saving goes through GO's own save, since normal browser downloads don't work in the Android app.

q: Why do Q-MEME memes have a Qortal logo on them?
a: Published memes carry the Qortal logo, which is what people see when a meme is pasted into a Qortal chat, and copies saved to a device carry qortal.dev instead. In the editor you can move, resize and turn the mark a little (up to 25 degrees either way), but it can't be removed.

q: Can I use animated GIFs in Q-MEME?
a: Yes. GIFs up to 2 MB, added as a meme or a template, are published exactly as they are. Bigger GIFs, up to 20 MB, are made smaller as GIFs so they keep moving. In the grid a GIF shows a still frame with a GIF badge: hover over it on a computer, or tap the badge on a phone, to play it.

q: How do I find memes in Q-MEME?
a: Library opens on Memes, with Templates beside it. Both sort by Top (most hearts) or New, filter by search words, and load more as you scroll. Tap the heart under a meme to like it.

q: How do I remove a meme I published in Q-MEME?
a: Open Mine, where your memes and templates are listed, and remove it there; you can also copy or edit them. Removing a post hides it from the library; it is not deleted from QDN. Only the registered name Q-MEME, the app's publisher, can remove other people's posts or block a name, from the Moderate tab.

q: Can I share several files at once in Q-Drive?
a: Yes. Select the files and choose Share in the selection bar: one share can hold up to 500 files, all for the same person, and it still costs 0.02 QORT. For more files, make a second share. Each share gives the person the keys to those files only.

q: How do I see who I shared a file with in Q-Drive?
a: Open Shared, then By me: each card shows who it was for, what it held and when, with a chip saying In their Shared, Link only or Stopped. A file's Details also names everyone it was shared with, including stopped shares.

q: Why does Q-Drive warn about hidden characters in a name?
a: A name with hidden or look-alike characters may be pretending to be someone else. Q-Drive strikes such a name through and warns you, both when you type a recipient and when a share comes from one. Check the person's address with them, by another way you trust, before you share or open anything.

q: Why does Hub ask me several times when I publish in Q-Drive?
a: Q-Drive sends small files together, so Hub usually asks once. Files too big to send together are asked for one by one, plus once more to save your file list, and a folder publish asks once per folder. The publish confirmation tells you how many times Hub will ask. Each file still costs 0.01 QORT.

q: Can I cancel or retry a publish in Q-Drive?
a: The transfer card at the bottom lists each publish and download with its step, such as Encrypting, Waiting for Hub or Publishing. You can cancel one that hasn't reached Hub yet, and Retry a failed one. "Not confirmed yet" means Hub's answer didn't arrive in time: tap Check again rather than publishing twice.

q: How do I change how Q-Drive looks?
a: Go to Settings, Appearance. Pick a theme (Hub 3.0 and Q-Drive Classic follow Hub's light or dark mode), show folders as a List or a Grid with previews, and choose Comfortable or Compact density. These choices are saved on that device only.

q: Where can I see what's new in Q-Drive?
a: Open Settings and scroll to About. It shows the version, says the app is published on Qortal under the name Q-Drive, and has What's new with the changes in each release.

q: Why does Subscreen ask me to confirm in Hub several times?
a: A title is several small QDN resources: the video, its details, and maybe a trailer and cast & crew. When there are too many to send at once, Qortal Hub asks you to confirm in a few rounds, about a minute apart, while the network catches up. The Ready to publish summary tells you how many times before you start.

q: How do I add a trailer on Subscreen?
a: Add a trailer while publishing (it is recommended and published with your title), or later on the title page under Trailer with "Publish a short video so people can preview this title". Confirm the file in Qortal Hub and keep Subscreen open until it finishes. A trailer adds one resource (0.01 QORT) to the fee.

q: What does Preview mode mean in Subscreen?
a: Preview mode is what you get when Subscreen runs outside Qortal Hub. You pick a display name with Continue locally and can try ratings, credits and publishing, but everything is saved in that browser only. Open Subscreen in Qortal Hub or GO to publish to QDN for real.

q: Can I watch the next episode automatically on Subscreen?
a: Yes. When an episode ends, Subscreen shows Next episode with a Play now button, so you can go straight on through a series.

q: What is the pop-out player in Subscreen?
a: Tap Pop out player in the player to keep the video playing in a small window you can drag around while you browse other pages in Subscreen. The title page then says Playing in pop-out, and Return player here brings it back into the page.

q: How do I pick a version when a movie has several copies on Subscreen?
a: Copies of the same movie from different publishers are combined into one card. On its title page, use the version choice to pick whose copy to play, for example a better quality one. Quality is estimated from each video's size and length when its file name claims more.

q: Can I move my video to another Q-Tube category from Subscreen?
a: Yes: Edit the title and pick a category under "Other Q-Tube categories (leaves Subscreen)". That republishes the video's details with the new category (0.01 QORT); the video file isn't published again. Subscreen then stops listing it, so moving it back is only possible from Q-Tube, by choosing Movies or Series there.

q: Can I change my QWB website after publishing it?
a: Yes. Open QWB with the same name, use Load saved draft if needed, make your changes and tap Publish Website again. The new version replaces the old one under the same qortal://WEBSITE/<name> link, and other nodes pick it up after a short while.

q: How do I add a map with pins to my QWB website?
a: Add the Map pins block. For each pin enter the latitude and longitude in decimal degrees, a title, and optionally a description, a photo and a colour, then set the map height and starting zoom. The map is served from QDN, and visitors click a pin to see its popup.

q: How do I let visitors join my group from my QWB website?
a: Add the Groups block and pick a group you belong to as the target (connect your wallet so QWB can list your groups). The published site shows the group's member count, refreshed at the interval you set, and authenticated visitors can ask to join it.

q: How do I add articles or a blog to my QWB website?
a: Add the Articles block for long-form articles with comment threads. You can link it to a Q-Blog: new articles can also be published to Q-Blog, and auto-sync can pull new Q-Blog posts into the block. Visitors can open each article in Q-Blog too.

q: What is the Countdown block in QWB?
a: Countdown shows a timer counting down to a date you set, for example a launch or an event, and can run an action when it reaches zero. Add it from Add blocks like any other block.

q: What is the Folders block in QWB?
a: Folders is a file library for your site. You can add files you already published on Q-Share by pasting their Q-Share link, or publish new ones to Q-Share, Q-Tube or Q-Music from the block. Visitors get an image gallery with Prev and Next, a PDF viewer with Light, Dim and Smart themes and zoom, and audio that plays as a playlist.

q: What is Discover snapshot in QWB settings?
a: With "Discover snapshot, list in catalog when I publish" on, each publish saves a picture of your homepage to QDN so other QWB users can find your site in Discover Templates and use it as a starting point. Turn it off to stay out of that catalog; visitors can still use "Use this website as your template" from your published site's account menu.

q: Why can't an app embedded in my QWB site sign in?
a: First tap Authenticate on the website itself: only then can the embedded apps share the session. If an app inside the page still can't sign in, that is often a Hub limit for apps inside other pages. Use Open in Qortal on the app's tile to open it in its own tab.

q: Can I turn off live clock-in sharing in POS+?
a: Yes. In Settings, Shifts, turn off "Share clock-ins live" if you'd rather not approve a publish for every clock-in. Hours are then published with the day close instead, so the owner's Live now list won't show them until then.

q: What does Clear saved copies do in POS+?
a: Settings, This device, Clear saved copies removes the store data POS+ cached on that device, so it loads fresh from QDN next time. Unpublished sales are never touched by it, so today's sales stay until you close the day.

q: Can I use POS+ on a phone or tablet?
a: Yes. POS+ runs inside Qortal GO on Android phones and tablets as well as in Qortal Hub on a computer, with layouts for each. Each device keeps its own sales draft for its location until you close the day there, so set Settings, This device, Location on every device you sell from.

q: Which places get the most detailed forecast in Q-Weather?
a: Hour-by-hour high-resolution regional models cover the USA (including Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico), Canada, Iceland, the UK and Ireland, the Nordic and Baltic countries, Poland and much of Europe, and coarser regional data covers Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. Everywhere else, and after the first two to three days, the forecast is ECMWF up to 15 days. Tap the model name on the map to see which model covers which hours for your place; How Q-Weather works lists the models in the forecast your node has.
source: QDN APP Q-Weather 1.0.5 (published bundle, How Q-Weather works) (region strings)

q: Does Q-Weather track my location?
a: No. Q-Weather talks only to your own Qortal node: it never contacts an outside server, needs no account and doesn't track you. You add your places yourself, by search or on the map, and your places and settings stay on your device.
source: QDN APP Q-Weather 1.0.5 (published bundle, How Q-Weather works) (howQdn)

q: How do I share a place from Q-Weather?
a: Open the place's ⋮ menu. Share copies a link to that place's forecast, and the same menu has Rename, Edit place, Delete place and Show in GO widgets.
source: QDN APP Q-Weather 1.0.5 (published bundle, How Q-Weather works) (place menu strings)

q: How do I message someone on ThankQ?
a: Open their listing or profile and tap Send Message, write it and Send. ThankQ sends it as a Q-Chat direct message and as a Q-Mail, so the person sees it even if they don't open ThankQ. Requests you send are announced to the other person the same way.

q: Where do I see my bookings on ThankQ?
a: Requests lists Incoming and Outgoing requests with their status, and a badge shows new incoming ones; while ThankQ is open it also pops up "New incoming request from" the guest. Your Profile has a calendar marking check-in and booked days, with your upcoming bookings under it.

q: How do I comment on a place in World Map?
a: Open the place, go to Comments, write your comment and tap Post, then confirm in Hub. The comment is published to QDN under your name, so you need a registered name, and anyone viewing the place can read it.

q: Can I use World Map on my phone?
a: Yes. In Qortal GO, World Map has tabs for Map, My POI's, My Lists, Discover and Profile. To set a place, tap the map once or drag the red pin, and long-press a community score to see how it is worked out.

q: Can I buy from several shops at once on Q-Shops?
a: Yes. Your Q-Shops cart groups items by shop, and shipping and store-asset totals are worked out per shop at checkout. You pay each shop separately with Pay this shop, approving each payment in Hub.

q: How do shop owners see orders made in Q-Shops?
a: Sign in with the name that publishes the shop, open the account menu and choose Open Manage Sales for that name, then Refresh from QDN. It lists checkouts made in the Q-Shops app, read from buyers' encrypted receipts. Orders placed on your own website show in its Q-Shop block's Merchant tab instead.

q: How do I change the theme of my QWB website?
a: In QWB's Settings, pick the site Theme for the published page, Light or Dark. Single blocks can also have their own look under Block appearance in their Options. Publish the site again for visitors to see the change.

q: How do I add a photo album to my QWB website?
a: Add the Albums block and pick your photos. QWB publishes them to QDN in one batch, so Hub asks you once rather than for every picture. Choose a layout (grid, masonry, hero or carousel); visitors can open pictures in a lightbox, and the carousel has arrows, dots and swiping.
